glossary.tat: TAT (turnaround time) – time from sample collection to result validation. The median is robust to extreme values.
glossary.pathological: A result outside the reference interval for the patient's sex and age (flag L/H, critical LL/HH).
glossary.critical: A critical value endangers the patient; the laboratory must phone it to the physician immediately.
glossary.samples: Number of unique orders containing at least one result that matches the filters.
glossary.westgard: Westgard rules – a set of statistical rules for evaluating quality-control runs (e.g. 1-3s, 2-2s, R-4s, 10x).
glossary.egfr: eGFR – estimated glomerular filtration rate from creatinine, age and sex (CKD-EPI 2021 equation).
glossary.pointValue: Point value – how many CZK an insurer pays per procedure point. For laboratories it is set by the annual reimbursement decree.
glossary.breakEven: Break-even – the minimum volume at which revenue covers a method's fixed and variable costs.
glossary.histogram: A histogram shows how often values fall into each interval and reveals the shape of the distribution (e.g. skew in enzymes).
glossary.boxplot: A box plot summarises a distribution in five numbers and makes groups easy to compare.
glossary.criticalTarget: Recommended target: phone a critical value to the physician within 30 minutes of validation.
glossary.cv: Coefficient of variation = SD / mean × 100. Measures the imprecision (spread) of repeated control measurements.
glossary.bias: Bias = (control mean − target) / target × 100. Measures systematic deviation of the method.
glossary.leveyJennings: A Levey-Jennings chart plots control measurements over time against the target and ±1, 2 and 3 SD bands.
glossary.percentile: 90th percentile = the value below which 90 % of samples fall. It shows the long tail of slow samples better than the mean.
glossary.ecdf: Empirical cumulative distribution: for each time, the share of samples that already have a result.
glossary.sankey: A Sankey diagram shows flows between states; band width is proportional to the number of results.
glossary.deltaCheck: A delta check compares a result with the same patient's previous result. An unexpectedly large change may indicate a sample mix-up or pre-analytical error.
glossary.pearson: Pearson's r measures a linear relationship (−1 to +1). For skewed data it is computed on logarithms.
glossary.spearman: Spearman's ρ is a rank correlation – robust to outliers and to non-linear (monotonic) relationships.
glossary.r2: The coefficient of determination R² is the share of Y's variance explained by the regression on X.
glossary.mri: Minimum retesting interval (MRI) – the time before which repeating a test usually adds no new information (e.g. HbA1c 90 days).
glossary.costPerResult: Estimate: number of early repeats × actual cost per reportable result of that test from the cost model.
glossary.procedures: A procedure = a reported test result the lab bills to an insurer (points) or to a self-payer.
glossary.absorption: Costs are assigned to reported results: number of results × the method's actual cost per result in that month (absorption costing).
glossary.costPerReportable: Actual cost per reportable result = all method costs (reagents, QC, calibration, expiry, EQA, staff, lease, overhead) / number of reported results.
glossary.pareto: The 80/20 Pareto rule: a small share of items often drives most of the effect. Sorted bars with a cumulative line show how many methods make up 80 %.
glossary.payback: Payback period = one-off introduction costs (validation, training) / monthly operating margin.
glossary.sensitivity: Sensitivity analysis shows which assumptions move the result most. The longest bars are the parameters to verify most carefully.
glossary.makeOrBuy: Make-or-buy compares running a method in-house with sending samples to a reference laboratory. When sent out, the reference lab bills the procedure; we keep only the pre-analytics and transport cost.
glossary.lifecycleLoss: Sum of negative cumulative results of discontinued methods: revenue − all costs including validation, training and expiry.
glossary.waterfall: A waterfall chart shows how a starting value changes step by step through positive and negative items to the final value.
glossary.annualized: Period result scaled to 12 months: result / number of months × 12.
glossary.breakEvenPointValue: By how much the point value would have to change (with the other scenario assumptions) for the operating result to be exactly zero.
glossary.holtWinters: Holt-Winters exponential smoothing tracks the level, trend and seasonality of a series, weighting older data less; α, β and γ are chosen by the lowest error.
glossary.mape: MAPE = mean absolute percentage error. The model is trained without the latest months and compared with what actually happened.

er.title: Data model – star schema
er.intro: Fact tables (events: orders, results, QC runs, monthly costs) link to dimensions (lookups: patients, tests, departments, insurers, analysers, calendar) through foreign keys. Numbers in the header = row count.
er.wideNote: For fast filtering the app builds denormalised tables results_wide, costs_wide and qc_wide (facts joined with dimensions) after loading, so all charts share the same WHERE condition.

about.intro: Where the dashboard's numbers come from, what is real and what is made up, and which simplifications the model makes.
about.disclaimerTitle: All patients, volumes and costs are fictional
about.disclaimer: The data were produced by a script with a fixed seed. They do not represent any real laboratory, hospital or patient. Only the public tariff data (procedure points, point value) and professional principles (reference intervals, Westgard rules, eGFR equation) are real.

vzp.name: VZP – Health procedures code list, version 1482
vzp.usage: Procedure codes and points for 45 tests (valid from Oct 1, 2026).

decree.name: Decree No. 432/2025 Coll. (2026 reimbursement decree)
decree.usage: Point value: CZK 0.80 (801, 813), 0.90 (818), 1.05 (999) for an accredited laboratory.

prices.name: Public self-payer price list (webkalkulacka.agellab.cz)
prices.usage: Self-payer prices – entered manually into data/source/ceny_samoplatci.csv; estimated from points until filled in.

mri.name: RCPath / ACB – National Minimum Retesting Intervals (2021)

ckdepi.name: Inker et al., NEJM 2021 – race-free CKD-EPI equation
ckdepi.usage: eGFR from creatinine, age and sex.

westgard.name: Westgard QC – Westgard Rules
westgard.usage: Rules for evaluating internal quality control.

real: Procedure codes and points from the VZP code list.
Point value for laboratory specialties from the 2026 reimbursement decree.
Reference and critical limits commonly used in clinical chemistry and haematology.
Insurers (codes and names) and the structure of orders, results and QC.
Professional methods: CKD-EPI 2021 eGFR, Westgard rules, minimum retesting intervals.
fictional: All patients, orders, results and their values.
Test volumes and their distribution over time.
Prices of reagents, QC, calibration, EQA, lease and overhead (realistic but made up).
Insurer contract coefficients on the point value (±3 %).
External clinics and their names, the method register and lessons learned.
Costs of sending samples to a reference laboratory.
generator: A Python generator (numpy, pandas, Faker cs_CZ) with a fixed seed of 42 creates 36 months of data (10/2023 – 9/2026): 5,000 patients, 50,000 orders, ~362,000 results, ~108,000 QC runs and monthly costs.

Orders are generated as care episodes (inpatient stays with daily draws, emergency visits, oncology cycles, outpatient visits). Values follow realistic distributions (log-normal for enzymes and CRP), seasonality (inflammation in winter, vitamin D in summer), correlations through shared clinical factors and a small share of haemolysed or faulty samples.
The cost model simulates reagents day by day, including expiry of opened packs. The result is the actual cost per reportable result, which rises steeply for low-volume methods.
simplifications: The BONlab laboratory coefficient and regulatory caps of the reimbursement decree are not modelled (revenue = points × point value).
When a sample is sent out, the reference lab bills the procedure; the lab keeps only the pre-analytics and transport cost.
Costs are assigned to results by absorption costing (results × the method's cost per result in the month).
STAT and routine runs of a test are billed under the same code.
Forecast and what-if are indicative decision models, not accounting predictions.
about.privacy: The app works with pseudonymised fictional data: instead of name and national ID only an ID, birth year and district. Everything runs locally in your browser – no data are sent to a server.
